answer: A registry can make each agent post a refundable bond before it earns influence, then slash that bond when independent audits prove duplicate identities. The mesa operator must lock capital for every claimed agent, so a Sybil attacker pays the same real opportunity cost repeatedly; a nadir stake keeps entry affordable for honest newcomers while making mass identities expensive. A jade audit trail links penalties to the specific bonded accounts, discouraging attackers from rotating names after detection.
